analysis.title: Sell Low, Buy High
key_insights: Tech sold off hard, volatility spiked and positioning was cut sharply. A squeeze followed as valuations started to look interesting.
NDX futures briefly dipped below the major trendline and are back above it. A very large upside candle is forming today. The 200-day MA remains higher.
US fundamental L/S gross leverage had its largest weekly decline since Covid, falling to 207.5% (26th percentile over the past year). Net leverage is at five-year lows.

Goldman's new Multiple Surprise Ratio (MSR) measures a daily move against the prior day's one-month implied volatility. SPX had its largest volatility-adjusted surprise in 19 years this week, NDX ranked in the top two and Russell 2000 in the top five. The options market underestimated the size of the moves.
Per DB, tech positioning is consistent with a sharp deceleration, outright negative growth and large estimate cuts.
Semis positioning cuts have pushed allocations back toward year lows.
SOX trades on a single-digit two-year forward P/E, per MS Alpha.

MS Alpha flagged NVDA near the top of its range with implied volatility at pre-COVID lows on September 23, favoring puts and AAPL calls versus NVDA puts as a relative trade. The trade has worked strongly and the note says to book profits.
Nvidia's share of Chinese data-center AI accelerator shipments fell to 34% in H1 2026, with Huawei at 28%. TS Lombard argues US export restrictions are speeding up China's domestic AI ecosystem.

TS Lombard says Chinese competitors only need to deliver sufficient compute at a lower price. With Nvidia gross margins near 75%, there is a large margin pool to attack, and cheaper power, domestic scale and better hardware could pressure Western AI economics.
JPM shows Asian tech ex-memory forward P/E near its long-term mean and price-to-book compressed while ROE stays elevated. The question is whether the earnings reset arrives.
